newsitem.title: USA: Senate farm panel to look at crop price volatility.
newsitem.headline: Senate farm panel to look at crop price volatility.

text.p: The Senate Agriculture Committee has scheduled a hearing on July 29 to look at the issue of commodity price volatility in the aftermath of the 1996 farm bill, the panel said Monday.

The committee will examine whether the 1996 farm bill has made farmers more vunerable to wide commodity price swings, as well as the proper role of the government in managing price volatility and preventing price manipulation.

In a speech to U.S. Agriculture Department overseas aides on Monday, Sen. Bob Kerrey, a Nebraska Democrat, noted that prospects for a large U.S. grain and soybean harvest this year have pushed commodity prices sharply lower.

Kerrey said it was unlikely that the price dip would prompt Congress to reopen the 1996 farm bill. But Kerrey said he still felt Congress made a mistake when it changed from a system of crop subsidy payments that rise and fall in response to market price to a system of fixed payments.
Other issues on the Senate farm panel agenda are:
--a hearing Wednesday on the contribution that ethanol and other alternative fuels can make to national energy security;
--a hearing July 22nd on the impact of newly proposed clean air regulations on the agriculture industry;
--a confirmation hearing July 23rd on the nominations of Catherine Wotecki to be USDA undersecretary for food safety and Shirley Watkins to be USDA undersecretary for Food and Consumer Services; and
--a July 31 hearing on the prospects for increasing U.S. agricultural exports to Africa.
